issue.body:
After trying to run eslint:

```
env: node\r: No such file or directory
```

`dos2unix` on entire `eslint` directory fixed problem

body: I'm not sure about automatically converting line-endings dos2unix only does one file at a time, so you have to pull each file individually into it. But to verify line-endings, we can just run eslint with `linebreak-style: [2, 'unix']`.

@ilyavolodin 
1. you could pass a whole dir to `dos2unix`. Something like:
    `
    find . -type f -print0 | xargs -0 dos2unix
`
2. You could use `sed`
3. To run `eslint` your `eslint` bin should work correctly :wink:

We can consume prepublish hook to run a script which can make sure all files have Unix line ending and if not make that change.
Now for the script part we can go with:
- [linefix](https://www.npmjs.com/package/linefix)
- [dos2unix for nodejs](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dos2unix)

@gyandeeps That's not really a problem. Problem is that if you modified something locally and then do `npm publish`, your modifications are not going through git at all, so autocrlf or precommit hook will not be launched. That's why it should be part of the release script, to convert line-endings locally (or at least warn about them) before doing `npm publish`.
Oh, sorry, I should read more carefully. Though you said `precommit` hook. But `prepublish` would do the trick. Didn't know about it. Problem with hooks though - they are hard to checkin to git.
Ok, I'll shut up and will go quietly read documentation in the corner before replying:-)
